options.title: Equipment loans database
options.pitch: Design a community equipment desk using invented borrowers and equipment.
requirements: Design Borrower, Category, Equipment and Loan entities, including repeat loans and optional return dates.
Explain the normalisation decisions, document keys/domains and create the relational database.
Implement joined loan reports, aggregate inventory reports and safe insert/update/delete operations. Test constraints and recovery.
resources: SQLite or school-approved RDBMS; DB Browser for SQLite is optional.
Included flat source CSV, relationship prompt and SQL TODO file.
Existing unit 2 workbook provides practice, not a private marking key.
tests: Borrower B01 and equipment E01 can have repeated loans with different loan IDs.
A loan referring to missing equipment is rejected when foreign keys are enabled.
Returned loans disappear from the active-loans report, while history remains.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

options.title: Community festival bookings
options.pitch: Manage fictional sessions, venues and participant bookings for a community festival.
requirements: Design Participant, Venue, Session and Booking entities, resolving participant-to-session multiplicity.
Document a normalised design, keys, domains and field-level validation before implementation.
Create joined booking reports and attendance totals. Demonstrate changes and test invalid references.
resources: SQLite; synthetic participants/session records; common design workbook.
Teacher supplies venue capacities and an unambiguous booking rule.
No online payments or real participant information.
tests: One participant can book different sessions but cannot duplicate the same booking.
Unknown participant/session references fail.
A session with no bookings behaves as the report specification states.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

options.title: Repair café register
options.pitch: Organise fictional repair appointments and equipment categories.
requirements: Model CustomerAlias, DeviceType, Device and Appointment with a documented scope.
Use a four-entity design, keys, relationships and normalisation evidence.
Produce joined appointment lists, totals by repair category and tested data changes.
resources: SQLite; invented records only; common test and data-dictionary templates.
No personal device contents, passwords or actual customer details.
Teacher supplies a small flat input table for normalisation.
tests: A device can have multiple appointments.
Deleting a referenced device follows an explicitly chosen integrity rule.
Totals match a small hand-counted fixture.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

options.title: VR lab loans and bookings
options.pitch: Use headset lending as a database context. Physical headsets are optional.
requirements: Model DeviceType, Device, BorrowerAlias and Loan in a normalised design.
Track invented asset labels and current loans without collecting headset-account information.
Produce available-device and overdue reports, demonstrate SQL changes and test referential integrity.
resources: SQLite plus a synthetic asset register; no Quest required.
Optional teacher demonstration of a real asset workflow.
Use the equipment pack structure with renamed fields and a fresh issued dataset.
tests: A returned device becomes available under the agreed rule.
An unknown asset ID fails validation.
The overdue-date boundary matches the written specification.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

options.title: VR lab booking and maintenance system
options.pitch: Develop an integrated Python/SQL system for a fictional shared-headset laboratory.
requirements: Model five related entities: BorrowerAlias, DeviceModel, Device, Booking and Maintenance. Explain keys, relationships and normalisation.
Create a Python interface that executes parameterised SQL for bookings, updates and reports. Include meaningful multi-table joins, grouped totals and calculated output.
Test integrity, a transaction that rolls back on failure, backup restoration and role/privacy decisions. Use synthetic asset and borrower data.
resources: Python sqlite3 and SQLite; no headset needed to earn any mark.
Included devices.csv, borrowers.csv, bookings.csv, schema-todo.sql and app-todo.py.
Optional headset observation only after school approval.
tests: A booking for an unknown device fails referential integrity.
A duplicate/conflicting booking follows the specified rejection rule.
A failed multi-step update rolls back and leaves earlier data unchanged.
routes: Python console interface using SQL: the baseline integrated solution.
Optional Python desktop GUI using the same database core.
Optional Python-backed local browser interface if already taught; retain the same SQL evidence.

options.title: Festival operations platform
options.pitch: Build integrated booking and reporting software for a fictional festival.
requirements: Design ParticipantAlias, Venue, Session, Booking and TicketType entities, with justified integrity constraints.
Implement a Python interface, parameterised SQL and joined/grouped operational reports.
Provide evidence for transaction failure, imported-data checks, recovery and access decisions.
resources: Python sqlite3, SQLite and synthetic data files.
No real payment or attendee data, and no live payment service.
Common normalisation, report-specification and recovery templates.
tests: Unknown foreign keys fail.
Booking totals and calculated revenue match a hand-computed fixture.
Simulated transaction failure restores the previous consistent state.
routes: Python console interface using SQL: the baseline integrated solution.
Optional Python desktop GUI using the same database core.
Optional Python-backed local browser interface if already taught; retain the same SQL evidence.

options.title: Repair and parts service
options.pitch: Integrate a repair queue, technician assignments and parts inventory.
requirements: Model CustomerAlias, Device, RepairJob, Part and JobPart as at least five related entities.
Implement Python workflows and SQL reports for open jobs, part usage and grouped totals.
Demonstrate referential/domain constraints, a stock/job transaction and a tested backup/restore procedure.
resources: Python and SQLite with synthetic job/stock data.
Teacher supplies stock rules and report requirements.
No actual customer devices, passwords or private customer data.
tests: A job with no parts stays visible in the defined operational report.
Insufficient stock rejects the transaction consistently.
A failed stock update does not leave an incorrect job total.
routes: Python console interface using SQL: the baseline integrated solution.
Optional Python desktop GUI using the same database core.
Optional Python-backed local browser interface if already taught; retain the same SQL evidence.

options.title: Environmental experiment registry
options.pitch: Manage fictional experiments, sensors and observations with a Python database interface.
requirements: Model Site, SensorType, Sensor, Experiment and Observation entities with declared dependencies.
Import a small deliberately imperfect synthetic CSV, retain the raw original and justify corrections.
Implement validated CRUD and joined/grouped reports. Evaluate data quality, integrity, transactions and recovery.
resources: Python, SQLite, teacher-created synthetic readings and common data-quality log.
No physical sensor is necessary.
Avoid inferring scientific validity from a working database.
tests: Reject unknown sensor IDs and values outside the declared domain.
A legitimate unusual reading remains distinguishable from an invalid record.
Reimport policy prevents unintended duplicate observations.

Optional Python desktop GUI using the same database core.
Optional Python-backed local browser interface if already taught; retain the same SQL evidence.

requirements: Suggested school paper: 10 minutes reading plus 3 hours working. Use a 40% short-answer and 60% extended-answer balance, with new original stimuli.
Sample Units 3–4. Build a content/demand/marks matrix and an item-specific key.

Prepare accessible diagrams, checking time and an independently moderated marking guide. The Year 12 external design specifies 10 minutes reading plus 3 hours working, 20–30 short questions and 4–6 extended questions.
resources: Included exam blueprint CSV and paper-review checklist.
Current syllabus examination design brief and school examination procedures.
Existing open practice papers are revision resources, not secure full exams.
tests: Check content coverage, question count, section totals and realistic timing.
Trial every code/SQL stimulus and verify all computed answers independently.
